title: Premature Write-Ahead Log for Transient In-Memory Caches
pattern: Writing all transactions, updates, or caching inserts to a write-ahead log (WAL) on disk for a transient, ephemeral caching server.
why_bad: Write-ahead logging and disk sync/fsync operations are incredibly slow, taking 5–10 ms (compared to nanoseconds for in-memory writes). If the cache is transient and does not require ACID durability, disk-based log files ruin performance [84].
detection: The presence of file append and fsync loops inside key-value storage or caching engines that are designated for temporary memory-only caching.
counterexample: Persistent database engines (like Postgres or RocksDB) where strict ACID durability is a core system requirement. `Contextual`.
fix: Disable logging and disk synchronization for transient nodes, allowing the cache to run entirely in RAM at peak speeds.
